title: Derived Hom continuity for relatively perfect coefficients
statement:
Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed poset, let $(R_i)_{i\in I}$ be a diagram of commutative rings, and let $R=\varinjlim_i R_i$ be its ring colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Fix $i_0\in I$ and a flat finitely presented homomorphism $R_{i_0}\to A_{i_0}$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map, def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. For $i\ge i_0$ put $A_i=A_{i_0}\otimes_{R_{i_0}}R_i$ and put $A=A_{i_0}\otimes_{R_{i_0}}R$. Use ordinary module derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and derived extension of scalars [def-trf-affine-diagonal-module-data]. Let $K_0,L_0\in D(A_{i_0})$. Assume $K_0$ is pseudo-coherent over $A_{i_0}$ [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex], and $L_0$ has finite Tor amplitude over $R_{i_0}$: there are integers $a\le b$ such that $H^n(L_0\otimes_{R_{i_0}}^{\mathbf L}Q)=0$ for every $R_{i_0}$-module $Q$ and $n\notin[a,b]$. Set $K_i=K_0\otimes_{A_{i_0}}^{\mathbf L}A_i$, $L_i=L_0\otimes_{A_{i_0}}^{\mathbf L}A_i$, and similarly $K,L$ over $A$. Then the canonical homomorphism
$$\varinjlim_{i\ge i_0}\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A_i)}(K_i,L_i)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(K,L)$$
is an isomorphism of abelian groups. The transition maps and the displayed map send a derived morphism to its derived scalar extension. No flatness of the transition homomorphisms $R_i\to R_j$ or $R_i\to R$, Noetherianity, or perfectness of $K_0$ over $A_{i_0}$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0DHX, lemma-colimit-relatively-perfect, part (2); restricted to small directed posets, with the canonical transition maps explicit.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-relative-rhom-flat-base-change-model] to $R_{i_0}\to A_{i_0}$ and $K_0,L_0$. Its hypotheses are precisely flatness, pseudo-coherence of $K_0$, and the given finite $R_{i_0}$-Tor interval for $L_0$; it does not require $L_0$ to be pseudo-coherent. Choose its $P_0,F_0$ and set $E_0=\operatorname{Hom}_{A_{i_0}}^\bullet(P_0,F_0)$. For every $R_{i_0}$-algebra $T$, its comparison gives $H^0(E_0\otimes_{R_{i_0}}T)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A_{i_0}\otimes_{R_{i_0}}T)}((K_0)_T,(L_0)_T)$. These comparisons intertwine every $T\to U$ with the derived scalar-extension map, including nonflat maps.

proof.text: Let $J=\{i\in I:i\ge i_0\}$. It is small, nonempty (contains $i_0$), and directed: a common upper bound of two elements of $J$ remains in $J$. Its ring colimit is $R$. Indeed a cocone on $J$ extends to $I$ by sending $R_i$ through any $R_j$ with $j\ge i,i_0$; two choices agree at a common upper bound, and these extensions are mutually inverse to restriction. The same universal-property argument identifies the ring colimit with the colimit in $R_{i_0}$-algebras: the structure map is the leg at $i_0$, and compatible legs respect it. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-underlying-module] over $R_{i_0}$ to conclude that $R$, with these legs, is also the colimit of the underlying $R_{i_0}$-modules $R_i$, $i\in J$.

source.place: Tag 0DHX, lemma-colimit-relatively-perfect, proof of (2), using Tag 0E1U (lemma-compute-RHom-relatively-perfect) and Tag 00DB (algebra-lemma-directed-colimit-exact).

proof.text: On the one-object site with only the maximal covering sieve, sheaves of $R_{i_0}$-modules are ordinary $R_{i_0}$-modules: there are no nontrivial restriction or sheaf conditions. Regard each $R_i$ as a complex concentrated in degree zero, and use the fixed complex $E_0$ in [lem-pc-module-filtered-colimits-tensor]. Step 2 identifies their termwise colimit with $R[0]$. The cited tensor-totalization comparison therefore gives a chain isomorphism $\varinjlim_{i\in J}(E_0\otimes_{R_{i_0}}R_i)\cong E_0\otimes_{R_{i_0}}R$. Here totalization with a degree-zero complex is ordinary termwise tensor; flipping the two factors sends $x\otimes r$ to $r\otimes x$ with no sign since $r$ has degree zero. The comparison sends the class of $x\otimes r_i$ to $x\otimes\iota_i(r_i)$ and commutes with the differential $d(x)\otimes r_i$. Thus it is the comparison induced by the actual scalar-extension chain maps. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful](3), this module-colimit cocone is also a colimit of the underlying abelian groups in each degree; its sheafification hypothesis holds because sheafification on this site is the identity.

proof.text: Put $C_i=E_0\otimes_{R_{i_0}}R_i$, $Z_i=\ker(d:C_i^0\to C_i^1)$ and $B_i=\operatorname{im}(d:C_i^{-1}\to C_i^0)$, all regarded as abelian groups. The chain maps make these compatible systems. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-abelian-groups-exact] to $0\to Z_i\to C_i^0\to C_i^1$, to $C_i^{-1}\to B_i\to0$, and to $0\to B_i\to Z_i\to H^0(C_i)\to0$. Exactness identifies $\varinjlim Z_i$ with the cycles in $\varinjlim C_i$, $\varinjlim B_i$ with its boundaries (using the injectivity into $\varinjlim Z_i$), and their quotient with $\varinjlim H^0(C_i)$. Therefore the canonical cocycle map $\varinjlim H^0(C_i)\to H^0(\varinjlim C_i)$ is an isomorphism. Combine it with the chain isomorphism of step 3 to obtain $\varinjlim_{i\in J}H^0(E_0\otimes R_i)\cong H^0(E_0\otimes R)$.

source.place: Tag 0DHX, lemma-colimit-relatively-perfect, proof of (2), using Tag 0E1U (lemma-compute-RHom-relatively-perfect) and Tag 00DB (algebra-lemma-directed-colimit-exact).

proof.text: Insert the isomorphisms of step 1 with $T=R_i$ and $T=R$ into step 4. For $i\le j$ in $J$, the chain map $h\otimes r_i\mapsto h\otimes\overline r_i$ induces, by the model's transition clause, the given map $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A_i)}(K_i,L_i)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A_j)}(K_j,L_j)$. The same clause for $R_i\to R$ identifies every colimit leg with derived extension to $A$. Hence the composite isomorphism of step 4 is exactly the displayed canonical homomorphism, by the universal property of the colimit of abelian groups. Additivity follows from the additive cohomology identifications. This proves the stated isomorphism with all transition maps normalized.

lean.statement: theorem relativePerfectHom_filtered_colimit {I : Type u} [PartialOrder I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)] (F : I ⥤ CommRingCat.{u}) (i₀ : I) (A : CommAlgCat.{u} (F.obj i₀)) [Module.Flat (F.obj i₀) A] [Algebra.FinitePresentation (F.obj i₀) A] (K L : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A)) (hK : DerivedCategory.IsPseudoCoherent K) (hL : ∃ a b : ℤ, a ≤ b ∧ DerivedCategory.torAmplitudeIn (ModuleCat.{u} (F.obj i₀)) a b ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (algebraMap (F.obj i₀) A)).mapDerivedCategory.obj L)) : ∃ (H : Set.Ici i₀ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{u}) (e : ∀ i : Set.Ici i₀, H.obj i ≅ relativePerfectHomGroup A K L (relativePerfectRingAt F i₀ i)), (∀ (i j : Set.Ici i₀) (f : i ⟶ j) (m : H.obj i), (e j).hom (H.map f m) = relativePerfectHomMap A K L (relativePerfectRingTransition F i₀ (leOfHom f)) ((e i).hom m)) ∧ ∃ c : colimit H ≅ relativePerfectHomGroup A K L (relativePerfectRingLimit F i₀), ∀ (i : Set.Ici i₀) (m : H.obj i), c.hom (colimit.ι H i m) = relativePerfectHomMap A K L (relativePerfectRingToLimit F i₀ i) ((e i).hom m)
